title: Assassin's Creed II
provenance: Reported by arulagarwal (highball-db#1284, 2026-11-17), Apple M4 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, Highball 0.10.26, engine x64-crossover26.3-r31, DXVK, msync, rated 4 of 5: the Ubisoft Connect copy, a written report in the form's shape. Played until a crash, at 1728x1117 and 120 Hz with VSync on. Highball's session count only caught the 10 second AssassinsCreedII.exe stub, which hands off to AssassinsCreedIIGame.exe through Connect. Switching away with Cmd+Tab in fullscreen crashes the game, the DXVK log showing a texture created at 4294935456x4294935327, which the player traces to the minimized window's size. DXVK_FORCE_WINDOWED=1 forced a window the game never resized, so it was reverted. The environment Highball set up for Ubisoft Connect was on DXMT with sync off, and this Direct3D 9 game lagged there (the player says it fell back to Wine's own Direct3D) until the environment was switched to DXVK and msync. Ubisoft Connect installed and signed in on this engine with DXMT_ALLOW_CROSS_PROCESS_SWAPCHAIN=1, WINE_SIMULATE_WRITECOPY=1 and a pin to UbisoftConnect.exe added by hand, although its tile in Highball says Blocked. The first sign in attempts hit Ubisoft's 'Access is temporarily restricted' check, which cleared after a wait. Not verified by the maintainer. arulagarwal (highball-db#1320, 2026-11-19), Apple M4 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, Highball 0.10.26, engine x64-crossover26.3-r31, WineD3D, rated 4 of 5: the same player and copy, also posted as a comment on highball-db#1284 the same day. On DXVK, besides the Cmd+Tab crash, the game also closed by itself during play, after about 18 minutes in one session and 1.5 in the next, with no Wine fault, out of memory error or macOS crash report, the Ubisoft overlay off and the exe already large address aware. The texture error from the first report also shows early in sessions that kept running, so the player doubts it is what ends the game. With the environment on Wine's own Direct3D the game ran about 3 hours without a close, Cmd+Tab no longer crashed it and performance was fine, at 1728x1117 and 120 Hz in fullscreen. Cmd+Space now opens Spotlight over the game. While Ubisoft Connect was still running the change of mode didn't apply (Highball said the environment was not restarted), so the player had to exit Connect fully, after which the DXVK log stopped being written. The environment ran with sync off although msync was set, because Steam had started it first in the player's words, and it ran fine. The player now puts the earlier lag down mostly to the sync setting, and suggests Wine's own Direct3D over DXVK for this game.
notes: A Direct3D 9 game. Reported playable on an M4 Pro with the Ubisoft Connect copy on the Wine 11 engine r31. The player found Wine's own Direct3D (WineD3D) the better graphics mode: about 3 hours of play without a close, and Cmd+Tab no longer crashes the game (highball-db#1320). On DXVK, which the same player used first, switching away in fullscreen crashed it and it also closed by itself during play (highball-db#1284, highball-db#1320). After changing the graphics mode, exit Ubisoft Connect fully before starting the game again, or it keeps the old mode. The environment Highball sets up for Ubisoft Connect uses DXMT with sync off, which lagged in this game for that player at first.

knownIssues.symptom: On DXVK, switching away with Cmd+Tab in fullscreen crashes the game (M4 Pro, Wine 11 r31, highball-db#1284)
knownIssues.cause: the game resizes its render targets to the minimized window's size, per the player. The DXVK log shows a texture of 4294935456x4294935327. The player later saw the same error early in sessions that kept running, so it may not be what ends the game (highball-db#1320)
knownIssues.fix: Wine's own Direct3D (WineD3D) as the environment's graphics mode, where Cmd+Tab no longer crashed it for the reporter (highball-db#1320). On DXVK, don't switch away while playing, save first, and turn on Do Not Disturb so nothing takes focus. DXVK_FORCE_WINDOWED=1 forces a window, but the game doesn't resize it

knownIssues.symptom: On DXVK the game closes by itself during play, without switching away, after about 18 minutes in one session and 1.5 in the next (M4 Pro, Wine 11 r31, highball-db#1320)
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. The player found no Wine fault, no out of memory error and no macOS crash report, with the Ubisoft overlay off
knownIssues.fix: Wine's own Direct3D (WineD3D), where the same player played about 3 hours without a close

knownIssues.symptom: Laggy in the environment Highball sets up for Ubisoft Connect, which uses DXMT with sync off (M4 Pro, Wine 11 r31, highball-db#1284)
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. DXMT has no Direct3D 9, so the game falls back to Wine's own Direct3D, per the player, who first blamed that and later mostly the sync setting. Yet the 3 hour session on Wine's own Direct3D ran with sync off and ran fine (highball-db#1320)
knownIssues.fix: the reporter first set the environment to DXVK and msync, then to Wine's own Direct3D, which played well (highball-db#1320)

knownIssues.symptom: After a change of graphics mode the game keeps the old one while Ubisoft Connect is still running, and Highball says the environment was not restarted (M4 Pro, highball-db#1320)
knownIssues.cause: the game starts through Connect, which keeps the environment running, per the player
knownIssues.fix: exit Ubisoft Connect fully, not just its window, then start the game again. The player saw the DXVK log stop being written after that

knownIssues.symptom: On Wine's own Direct3D, Cmd+Space opens Spotlight over the game (M4 Pro, highball-db#1320)
knownIssues.cause: macOS shortcuts aren't blocked there as they were with DXVK in fullscreen, per the player
knownIssues.fix: harmless. Spotlight's shortcut can be changed in System Settings
